messages:
beta_customer_inc: Heads up — after bumping redwood-python from 1.9.2 -> 1.11.0 our service started getting TypeError on start: 
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'session_timeout'

marta: thanks for reporting. can you paste the minimal repro and the sdk version from pip freeze?

beta_customer_inc: pip freeze shows redwood==1.11.0, other deps unchanged. repro is tiny:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=env('REDWOOD_KEY'), session_timeout=30)
```
instantly fails on import/construct. used to work on 1.9.2

ryan: this is expected if you relied on the old alias — we removed `session_timeout` in 1.10 in favor of `timeout` to align naming. Should have been in the changelog but i'll double-check.

beta_customer_inc: ouch. would have been nice to know, this broke a production deploy. any quick mitigation other than changing code everywhere?

jamal: short-term: pin to 1.9.x in your requirements.txt: `redwood==1.9.2` until you can migrate. We've seen a few customers hit this. long-term: update to `timeout=` arg.

marta: can you share the exact error / stacktrace? and are you using the SDK via a vendor image (we've seen pinned deps too)?

beta_customer_inc: full stack (sanitized):
```
File "/app/main.py", line 3, in <module>
  from redwood import Client
File "/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
  from .client import Client
File "/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/client.py", line 45, in <module>
  class Client(BaseClient):
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'session_timeout'
```

alex: that stack suggests the param alias removal changed the base signature; we might still accept aliases but doesn't look like it. i'll open a tiny patch to restore backwards-compatible alias for 1.11.x as a hotfix.

ci-bot: deploy request created: #PR-4521 (redwood-sdk: add deprecated alias for session_timeout) — triggered test matrix

ryan: ETA for hotfix? tests are running but we can cut a patch if CI passes in ~30-45m. will post back.

beta_customer_inc: thanks — we'll pin for now. also saw some retry behavior changes after 1.10 where we got 429s more often — any known related changes?

jamal: 1.10 changed default retry backoff and introduced a slightly stricter default max-concurrency to protect servers; that can increase client-side 429s if you had tuned batching assumptions. If you pinned 1.9 you should see previous behaviour.

marta: for customers that can't pin, short-term workarounds:
- use `timeout=` instead of `session_timeout` to be future-proof
- configure `Client(retry_policy={"max_retries": 3, "backoff_factor": 0.5})` if you rely on old pacing
- set `max_concurrency` in client config to match previous envs

beta_customer_inc: appreciated. also any guidance for detecting these breaking changes earlier? we didn't have a failing test for client init.

ryan: we'll add a migration note to the changelog and create a compatibility test in CI that imports common init patterns from our integration test matrix. also recommend you run `pip list --outdated` across envs or lock via `pip-compile`/poetry.

alex: PR passed CI and i cut 1.11.1 with alias restore; patch release notes: "temporary backwards-compatible alias: session_timeout -> timeout; please migrate to `timeout` and pin only until full migration"

ci-bot: release published: redwood 1.11.1 (sha: abc123hotfix)

beta_customer_inc: we upgraded to 1.11.1 and can confirm startup no longer crashes. we'll plan code updates next sprint. thanks for the fast turnaround :thumbsup:

marta: sorry for the disruption — we'll follow up with a proper deprecation notice and migration guide in the docs and add better migration tests.

ryan: also sending a brief note to customers who installed 1.10+ without pinning.

jamal: closing loop: if you hit the 429s after upgrading, post a sample trace and request pattern and we'll advise on `max_concurrency` + retry config.

beta_customer_inc: will do. thanks everyone.
